action: Microsoft says this was not an attack, so no security action is needed. General advice: confirm that delayed email has arrived, check your agreement for service credits and review how staff communicate when email is down.
exec: A prolonged email and collaboration outage shows dependence on one cloud supplier; Microsoft says it was not an attack.
impact: Outlook, Teams and Copilot were disrupted in 74 countries; per CyberCube the broader incident lasted about 38 hours.
plain: A fault on November 12 took down Outlook and disrupted Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft services in 74 countries. Microsoft's report says its testing missed the hardware and traffic mix involved; it says this was not an attack.

evidence.quote: "Our testing did not adequately represent the combination of hardware and traffic mix encountered during this incident," Microsoft said in the report.
will most likely total less than $100 mn, according to its preliminary catastrophe analysis.

Outlook, Teams and Copilot remain disrupted in 74 countries.
Severe disruption lasted approximately 18 hours, while the overall incident continued for about 38 hours.

summary: Outlook, Teams and Copilot were disrupted from 12 November in 74 countries, per Al Jazeera; CyberCube puts the broader incident at about 38 hours. Microsoft's report says its testing did not adequately represent the hardware and traffic mix encountered (KIRO 7). Digital Daily and Cyber Security News, relaying Reuters, say Microsoft declared an internal "Code Red" afterwards, aiming to restore services within one hour of any future incident.
title: Microsoft 365 outage knocks out Outlook, Teams and Copilot in 74 countries

validation.note: Al Jazeera (13 Nov) and KIRO 7 (21 Nov, Microsoft's report) each state the outage and that it was not a cyberattack; Beinsure relays CyberCube's estimates. BleepingComputer returned 403 and was not read; the Yahoo Finance roundup was removed as a source.
